h: פָּרָשַׁת כִּי תָבוֹא, ב׳ Ki Savo, 2
First Fruits and the Joy of Recognizing the Giver

p: "And it shall be, when you come," etc.
We must understand the expression "and it shall be,"
that it is said in connection with a mitzvah;
only when it wishes to state a promise
is the expression "and it shall be" fitting:
in such a manner He promises such,
"And it shall be, because you listen," etc.,
the expression "and it shall be" does not fit.
And if it refers to what is said,
"and you possess it and dwell in it"
in the passage of Ki Seitzei too it is written
"and Hashem your God delivers him into your hand,"
and nevertheless it is not written
"and it shall be, when you go out,"
but only "when you go out," etc.,
to the mitzvah of the captive woman;
"and you shall take of the first," etc.
But the expression "and it shall be"
refers to the conclusion of the passage,
"And you shall rejoice in all the good," etc.;
which is the first for Hashem,
And as for its saying "in all the good":
"And not everyone is for gladness, etc.;
"and for the upright of heart, gladness";
when one merits to straighten the heart,
And surely Hashem Yisbarach did not command
but only the joy that comes
so that they merit to remove the yetzer hara
And this is what it says:
"And you shall rejoice in all the good,"
And this is what it says (Devarim 26:3):
"I declare today to Hashem your God," etc.;
yet he has not yet declared anything,
for this is the beginning of the recitation!
the first fruit of the ground to Hashem,
that he recognizes the power of the Giver:
"that I have come to the land
which Hashem swore to our fathers
that they are only from the side of good,
and there is in them no admixture of evil at all.
in which one thanks and recognizes
that Hashem Yisbarach is the One who feeds and sustains,
"And you shall eat and be satisfied, and bless
"Take heed lest your heart be enticed,"
in the passage of "Vehayah im shamoa" (Devarim 11:16),
after "and you shall eat and be satisfied"
and in the Sifrei on Eikev
and so it is in the Gemara and the holy Zohar;
for by recognizing the power of the Giver,
the food will no longer bring
to accusation by the yetzer hara.
the first of his fruit before Hashem
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה כְּבָר הִגַּדְתִּי וְגוֹ׳
and through this already "I declare," etc.,
that is, that he recognizes the power of the Giver
that they are only from the side of good,
the aspect of words of Torah,
And this is what it says afterward:
"And you shall rejoice in all the good,"
"and for the upright of heart, gladness";
and the eating will be "in all the good,"
the aspect of words of Torah:
are from the side of the Tree of Life,
in which the yetzer hara has no dominion,
and the eating of Shabbos helps
that it be from the side of good
and have no admixture of evil
or dominion of the yetzer hara,
And on Shabbos every one of Yisrael
is in the aspect of a talmid chacham,
with a hint from the Gemara (Shabbos 119a):
"Are you more important to us than she?"
And they said in the Gemara (Kesubos 105b):
"Whoever brings a gift to a talmid chacham
is as though he offered Bikkurim."
that it be only from the side of good,
and there will be "and you shall rejoice in all the good."
